claims.head: The Penguins should drive the play
claims.body: The Penguins have been near the top of the league at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Sharks one of the worst. Expect the Penguins to spend more of the night in the Sharks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

claims.head: Crash the net vs. Bombs away
claims.body: On shots from in close, Pittsburgh is the league’s best, but San Jose is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Penguins to do more of their damage around the net.

notes.text: Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 11 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Spencer Stastney has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 67% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 60:11 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 36:00 together.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 6 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 25% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Igor Chernyshov is on injured reserve and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Collin Graf has taken his spot beside Will Smith and Macklin Celebrini.
Alexander Wennberg is on injured reserve and has missed the last 9 games. He is a top-six forward.
Filip Bystedt was added to the roster on Oct 29 and has played beside Tyler Toffoli and Ivar Stenberg.
Eric Pohlkamp was added to the roster on Nov 4.

stakes: The Penguins go in tied for seventh in the Metropolitan with 12 points, the Sharks tied for fifth in the Pacific with 15 points.

SJS.head: The Sharks face a real test
SJS.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, Pittsburgh has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks can pull it off if they get good looks.

PIT.head: The Penguins have a lot going for them
PIT.body: Even though San Jose has home-ice advantage, Pittsburgh has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. The Sharks’ way back in is getting good looks.

story.head: Somebody has to win
paras: The Sharks are on a four-game losing streak, and the Penguins are winless in four (0-3-1). Both teams are near the bottom of the standings. Going in, the Pens are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Sharks sixth in the Pacific (tied for 24th).

The Penguins have played better than their record (.375) says: their chances are worth about .560, mostly because they’re 3-6 in one-goal games. The Sharks’ record (.417) is about what their chances are worth.

The Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest), get more of their shots from in close than anyone (1st) and rarely throw hits (lowest). The Sharks, by contrast, hit a lot (3rd). Pittsburgh has allowed 3.56 goals a game, the fourth most in the league. As for the Sharks, they ice the puck a lot (32nd). They also do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest), so the Penguins get in close, but them mostly shoot from distance. San Jose has scored 2.44 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Penguins could find some good looks against the Sharks, who give up plenty of them.

Erik Karlsson (3 G / 13 A / 16 P in 16 GP) leads the Penguins in scoring, and Nick Robertson (7 G / 0 A / 7 P in 16 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Sharks, Macklin Celebrini (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring.
Artūrs Šilovs (5-5-1 / .876 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for Pittsburgh, and Yaroslav Askarov (4-8-0 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) for San Jose.
The Penguins usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.
